storyTitle: As an Automotive Reporting Analyst, I want query results returned through an interactive interface with status feedback so that I can review PostgreSQL data efficiently and trust the reporting outcome

functional.title: Approved reporting request shows progressing execution states and then renders complete interactive PostgreSQL results with linked query context
preconditions: User is logged in with the Automotive Reporting Analyst role and is authorized for the automotive reporting domain tied to request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1001'.

An approved interpreted request with request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1001' exists in the AI query workflow and is configured to return a successful PostgreSQL result set with columns DealerName, VehicleVIN, WarrantyStatus, ClaimCount.
The governed query service is available and returns execution metadata including executionStatus, requestId, rowCount, columns, rows, and queryContext for the request.
The test environment supports network timing observation so the tester can verify that a visible status update or final results appear within 10 seconds under normal load.

steps.action: From the approved requests list, locate request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1001' and click the 'Open Results' action.
steps.expectedResult: The application opens a single results experience for request 'REQ-POSTGRES-1001' and displays an initial processing state instead of a blank page or editable SQL interface.

steps.action: Observe the results header and timing from the moment the results view opens for up to 10 seconds.
steps.expectedResult: Within 10 seconds, the interface shows a visible execution state such as 'Queued' or 'Running', or directly shows the final results if execution completes faster.

steps.action: Remain on the same results page without clicking any resubmit or refresh control and watch the status area until the request completes.
steps.expectedResult: The execution state updates in place from processing to 'Queued' and/or 'Running' and then to 'Completed' without requiring the user to resubmit the request and without opening a second request.

steps.action: After status changes to 'Completed', review the rendered results grid.
steps.expectedResult: A tabular results view appears showing column headers DealerName, VehicleVIN, WarrantyStatus, ClaimCount and returned row data; the interface also displays the request ID and a row count matching the result payload.

steps.action: In the completed results view, locate the query context section or expandable panel.
steps.expectedResult: The query context ties the displayed output to the executed SQL text or approved SQL summary and identifies the related PostgreSQL source objects such as schema and table/view names used for the request.

steps.action: Inspect the page for restricted controls and sensitive backend information.
steps.expectedResult: No direct SQL editing controls, unrestricted database access options, raw database credentials, connection strings, usernames, passwords, or host details are shown anywhere in the UI.

steps.action: Verify the final state by checking that the request summary, execution status, row count, and query context all remain visible together on the same page.
steps.expectedResult: The completed request remains stable in the interactive results experience with status 'Completed', correct row data, request metadata, and linked query context all visible and internally consistent.

postconditions: Request 'REQ-POSTGRES-1001' remains recorded as completed in the platform with its associated requestId, execution status, row count, and query context available for review.
The user remains authenticated and stays on the interactive results page for the approved request.
No duplicate execution is created as a result of status updates occurring in the same interface.

functional.title: Completed results support efficient analyst review through sortable tabular output while preserving request-level metadata and result linkage
preconditions: User is logged in as an Automotive Reporting Analyst with access to approved request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1002'.

Request 'REQ-POSTGRES-1002' has already completed successfully and returns at least 5 rows with mixed values in columns DealerName, ServiceDate, ClaimAmount, and VehicleVIN so sorting changes are observable.
The completed payload includes requestId, executionStatus 'Completed', rowCount, columns, rows, and queryContext.

steps.action: Open the results view for approved request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1002'.
steps.expectedResult: The page loads directly into a completed interactive results view showing the request ID, execution status 'Completed', row count, and the tabular dataset.

steps.action: Review the initial table content and note the first three values shown under the 'ClaimAmount' column.
steps.expectedResult: The table displays valid row data with readable column headings and enough rows to evaluate sorting behavior.

steps.action: Click the 'ClaimAmount' column header once.
steps.expectedResult: The table sorts the rows in one direction based on ClaimAmount values, and the ordering of the first rows changes accordingly while the same request ID and row count remain displayed.

steps.action: Click the 'ClaimAmount' column header a second time.
steps.expectedResult: The table reverses the sort order for ClaimAmount, proving the output is interactive and sortable without re-running the request.

steps.action: Click the 'DealerName' column header.
steps.expectedResult: The table sorts by DealerName, allowing a different review path while preserving the completed request state and the same dataset size.

steps.action: Open or review the query context panel after sorting.
steps.expectedResult: The executed SQL text or summary and source schema/table/view references remain tied to the same request and are not lost or changed by table sorting.

steps.action: Confirm the final state of the page after multiple sorts.
steps.expectedResult: The analyst can continue reviewing returned rows efficiently in the same results experience, with stable request metadata, completed status, and unchanged row count after all sorting actions.

postconditions: The completed result set for 'REQ-POSTGRES-1002' remains available and unchanged except for client-side sort order in the UI.
Request-level metadata and query context remain associated with the displayed rows throughout the review session.
No new execution or duplicate request submission is triggered by sorting interactions.

functional.title: Opening an approved request already in progress updates status in place to completed without duplicate submission or manual resubmission
preconditions: User is logged in as an Automotive Reporting Analyst with authorization to view request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1003'.

Approved request 'REQ-POSTGRES-1003' exists and is currently in an in-progress execution state in the governed query service, expected to move from 'Queued' to 'Running' and then 'Completed' during the test.
The results interface uses polling or push updates configured for normal operation.

steps.action: Navigate to the approved request list and open request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1003' by clicking 'Open Results'.
steps.expectedResult: The results page opens and shows the current in-progress state for the request rather than displaying stale final data.

steps.action: Observe the request state area for the first update cycle without clicking any retry, submit, or browser refresh control.
steps.expectedResult: The visible status shows 'Queued' or 'Running' and includes the same request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-1003'.

steps.action: Continue watching the same page until the next backend status transition occurs.
steps.expectedResult: The execution state updates in place to the next valid state and does not require the analyst to resubmit the request to see progress.

steps.action: Allow the request to complete naturally and watch the interface transition.
steps.expectedResult: When the backend reports completion, the status area is replaced by the final interactive results view on the same page.

steps.action: Verify the browser page, request header, and dataset after completion.
steps.expectedResult: Only one request ID is shown, the execution status is 'Completed', and one consistent result set is displayed with no indication that a second execution was created.

steps.action: Review the metadata section for execution details such as duration and row count if displayed.
steps.expectedResult: Request-level execution details are visible and tied to the same request that progressed through in-place status updates.

postconditions: Request 'REQ-POSTGRES-1003' is completed and visible in the interactive results interface.
The user session remains active on the same results page with no duplicate request submitted.
The status progression is reflected for auditability through the same request identifier.

negative.title: Unauthorized or invalid request access is blocked for results retrieval and no protected PostgreSQL output is exposed
preconditions: Two request IDs are available for testing: 'REQ-POSTGRES-2001' is valid but belongs to a different reporting domain than the logged-in user is authorized to access, and 'REQ-POSTGRES-XXXX' is a non-existent or invalid request ID.
User is logged in as an authenticated Automotive Reporting Analyst whose RBAC permissions do not include the domain for 'REQ-POSTGRES-2001'.
The application supports direct navigation to the results route or opening results from the request list.

steps.action: Attempt to open the results page directly for request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-2001' using the application route or UI action.
steps.expectedResult: Access to the results is denied; the user does not see tabular query data, executed SQL details, or source object information for the unauthorized request.

steps.action: Review the message presented after the unauthorized access attempt.
steps.expectedResult: The interface shows a user-safe access or authorization message and does not reveal sensitive implementation details, database credentials, or raw backend errors.

steps.action: Now attempt to open the results page for invalid request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-XXXX'.
steps.expectedResult: The application rejects the request as invalid or not found and does not render a completed results view.

steps.action: Inspect the page state and any metadata shown after the invalid request attempt.
steps.expectedResult: No rows, no misleading final status, and no query context are displayed for the invalid request; any message is non-technical and appropriate for a missing or invalid request.

steps.action: Return to the approved requests list or previous page.
steps.expectedResult: The user remains logged in and can continue normal authorized work without having gained access to unauthorized or invalid request data.

postconditions: No PostgreSQL result rows or protected query context are disclosed for either the unauthorized or invalid request.
The user session remains authenticated but constrained by RBAC permissions.
No execution is triggered for the unauthorized or invalid request IDs.

negative.title: Failed query execution shows clear non-technical failure messaging with request identifier and suppresses incomplete final results
preconditions: User is logged in as an Automotive Reporting Analyst authorized to access approved request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002'.

Approved request 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002' is configured in the test environment to fail during PostgreSQL execution and return executionStatus 'Failed' with a requestId and failure code from the governed query service.
No previously cached completed results exist for 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002' in the test browser session.

steps.action: Open the results view for approved request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002'.
steps.expectedResult: The page opens into a processing or in-progress state associated with request 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002'.

steps.action: Wait for the execution outcome to be returned by the service without refreshing or resubmitting the request.
steps.expectedResult: The visible state transitions to 'Failed' within the same interface when the backend reports failure.

steps.action: Read the message shown in the status or error area.
steps.expectedResult: A clear, non-technical failure message is shown along with the request identifier 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002'; the wording does not expose stack traces, SQL engine internals, or database connection details.

steps.action: Inspect the main content area where results would normally appear.
steps.expectedResult: The interface does not display partial row data or misleading completed results as if the request succeeded.

steps.action: Review the page for any editable SQL control or retry behavior that could imply unrestricted database access.
steps.expectedResult: No direct SQL editing controls or raw database access elements are presented in the failure state.

steps.action: Verify the final page state after the failure message is displayed.
steps.expectedResult: The request remains identifiable as failed, the failure state is stable, and the analyst has enough safe context to report or troubleshoot using the request ID.

postconditions: Request 'REQ-POSTGRES-2002' remains marked as failed and is not misrepresented as completed.
No partial or misleading final result set is shown for the failed request.
The user stays authenticated on a stable error state page containing the request identifier.

negative.title: Request exceeding the normal response window continues to show delay status with request identifier and does not present incomplete output as complete
preconditions: User is logged in as an Automotive Reporting Analyst authorized for approved request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-2003'.
Approved request 'REQ-POSTGRES-2003' is configured to exceed the normal 10-second response window while remaining in a non-completed execution state.
The governed query service returns requestId and current executionStatus updates for the delayed request.

steps.action: Open the results view for approved request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-2003' and start timing from the moment the page loads.
steps.expectedResult: The page shows an initial processing state for the request.

steps.action: Observe the status area continuously through the first 10 seconds without resubmitting the request.
steps.expectedResult: The user receives a visible processing update such as 'Queued' or 'Running' within the response window, or equivalent delay feedback, rather than being left with no indication of activity.

steps.action: Continue observing after the 10-second normal response window has passed.
steps.expectedResult: The interface shows a clear delay or still-processing message with request ID 'REQ-POSTGRES-2003' and does not switch to a misleading 'Completed' state.

steps.action: Inspect the results region while the request remains delayed.
steps.expectedResult: No incomplete output is presented as final tabular results; if placeholders are shown, they are clearly non-final.

steps.action: Verify the page for safe messaging and absence of sensitive backend details.
steps.expectedResult: The status communication remains user-safe, with no database credentials, connection details, raw SQL errors, or technical exception traces exposed.

steps.action: Confirm the end state of the delayed request view without manually resubmitting.
steps.expectedResult: The user remains on the same request page with an accurate in-progress or delayed status and request identifier, and no duplicate submission has occurred.

postconditions: Request 'REQ-POSTGRES-2003' remains in a non-completed state and is clearly labeled as delayed or still processing.
No final results are falsely displayed for the delayed request.
The analyst can reference the displayed request ID for follow-up without having created a duplicate execution.

edgeCases.title: Render a completed approved request that returns zero rows while preserving completed status, query context, and accurate row count
preconditions: User is authenticated as an Automotive Reporting Analyst with RBAC access to the target automotive reporting domain.
An approved interpreted request exists with a valid requestId that is configured to execute successfully against PostgreSQL and return zero rows.

The governed query service returns a completed payload containing requestId, executionStatus='completed', columns metadata, an empty rows array, and queryContext with executed SQL summary and source schema/table or view references.
User is on the approved request details page or workflow screen where the interactive results experience can be opened.

steps.action: Open the approved request using its valid requestId from the AI query workflow and start the interactive results view.
steps.expectedResult: The results interface opens for the selected request without exposing any SQL editing control, database credential field, or unrestricted database access option.

steps.action: Observe the request state while the page loads and wait for the execution outcome to be retrieved.
steps.expectedResult: The interface shows a processing state and then transitions to a visible completed state for the same request without requiring a second submission.

steps.action: Review the main results panel after the request reaches completed status.
steps.expectedResult: The interface shows the interactive results view with column headers present, no data rows displayed, and no placeholder partial data presented as if final results exist.

steps.action: Verify the row count and completion indicators in the results metadata area.
steps.expectedResult: The UI clearly indicates zero returned rows, the execution status remains completed, and the request identifier is visible and matches the opened request.

steps.action: Open or expand the query context section for the completed request.
steps.expectedResult: The query context ties the empty result set to the executed SQL text or SQL summary and the source PostgreSQL schema/table or view references used for the request.

steps.action: Inspect the full page for security-related exposure.
steps.expectedResult: No raw database credentials, connection strings, hostnames, passwords, or direct SQL editing controls are displayed anywhere in the completed zero-row experience.

postconditions: The request remains stored as completed for the same requestId.
No result rows are created or displayed for the request, and the UI accurately reflects a zero-row outcome.
The analyst remains on the interactive results view with request-linked query context visible or accessible.
No duplicate request execution is triggered by viewing the completed zero-row result.

edgeCases.title: Handle a successful request with a large result set by showing timely completion, stable tabular rendering, and usable sorting with full metadata
preconditions: User is authenticated as an Automotive Reporting Analyst with permission to view the automotive reporting request and its domain results.
An approved interpreted request exists with a valid requestId that is configured to execute successfully and return a large but supported dataset, such as 1000 or more rows across multiple columns.
The governed query service returns a valid completed payload containing columns, rows, executionStatus, requestId, and queryContext for the large result set.
Test environment is under normal operating conditions so status update or completed results should appear within the 10-second SLA.

steps.action: Open the approved request by requestId and start the interactive results experience.
steps.expectedResult: The page displays an initial processing indicator tied to the selected request and does not create a duplicate submission action.

steps.action: Measure elapsed time from opening the request until either a visible status update or the final results appear.
steps.expectedResult: A processing status update or final completed results become visible within 10 seconds under normal load.

steps.action: When results load, review the table structure, visible rows, and page responsiveness while scrolling within the result area.
steps.expectedResult: The large result set renders in an interactive tabular view with readable column headers, visible rows, and no broken layout, browser freeze, or incorrect status transition.

steps.action: Verify the metadata area for the completed request.
steps.expectedResult: The interface shows completed status, the correct requestId, and a row count consistent with the returned dataset rather than an obviously truncated or misleading total.

steps.action: Click one sortable column header, such as 'Dealer Name' or another available text column, to sort ascending, then click the same header again to sort descending.
steps.expectedResult: The table reorders rows correctly in each direction, the sorted state is visually indicated, and the request remains in completed status with no accidental re-execution.

steps.action: Open the query context section after sorting and review its content.
steps.expectedResult: Executed SQL text or summary and source schema/table or view references remain available and correctly associated with the same completed large-result request.

postconditions: The completed request remains associated with the large result set and its requestId.
The results table stays usable for analyst review after sorting, with no duplicate request submission triggered.
Query context remains linked to the same displayed results.
No database credentials or direct SQL editing controls are exposed in the interface.

accessibility.title: Verify full keyboard-only access through status, query context, and sortable results table without requiring a mouse
preconditions: User is authenticated as an Automotive Reporting Analyst and has access to a valid approved request that completes successfully with at least several rows of result data.
The request returns a completed payload with columns, rows, executionStatus, requestId, and queryContext.
A desktop browser supported by the application is opened with standard keyboard navigation enabled and no mouse interaction used during the test.

steps.action: Using keyboard only, navigate from the browser address bar into the interactive results page for the approved request and move focus through the page with Tab and Shift+Tab.
steps.expectedResult: All interactive controls in the results experience, including request navigation, query context toggle or link, and sortable column headers, are reachable in a logical focus order.

steps.action: Observe the focused element at each stop while tabbing through the page.
steps.expectedResult: A visible focus indicator is present on each interactive element, and focus is not hidden, lost, or trapped in any section of the page.

steps.action: Use Enter or Space on the control that opens or expands the query context section.
steps.expectedResult: The query context section opens or collapses using the keyboard only, and the resulting state change is visually clear without shifting focus unpredictably.

steps.action: Tab to a sortable table header and activate it with Enter or Space to sort the results, then activate it again to reverse the sort.
steps.expectedResult: The table sorts in response to keyboard activation, the sort state changes appropriately, and the interaction does not trigger a page refresh or request resubmission.

steps.action: Continue keyboard navigation through the results region after sorting, including moving to the next interactive control after the table header.
steps.expectedResult: Focus continues in a logical sequence after the sorting action and remains within the current page context, allowing the analyst to keep reviewing results.

steps.action: Complete the navigation flow to the end of the interactive results experience and then reverse through key controls with Shift+Tab.
steps.expectedResult: The entire core flow can be completed without a mouse, with no keyboard trap, no unreachable controls, and no loss of access to status, table, or query context content.

postconditions: The request remains completed and no duplicate execution is initiated by keyboard interactions.
The final table sort state reflects the last keyboard action performed.
The user remains on the interactive results page with keyboard access preserved across status, results, and query context areas.

accessibility.title: Verify screen reader announcements and semantic labeling for execution status changes, request identifier, query context, and results table
preconditions: User is authenticated as an Automotive Reporting Analyst and can access two approved requests: one that transitions from processing to completed and one that returns a failed or delayed outcome.
A screen reader such as NVDA, JAWS, or VoiceOver is enabled in a supported browser.
The completed request returns columns, rows, executionStatus, requestId, and queryContext; the failed or delayed request returns a user-safe message and requestId without partial final results.

steps.action: Open the request that starts in a processing state while the screen reader is running and listen to the page announcement when the results experience loads.
steps.expectedResult: The screen reader announces a meaningful page title or landmark and a clearly labeled processing status for the current request rather than unlabeled dynamic content.

steps.action: Remain on the page until the request status changes from queued or running to completed.
steps.expectedResult: The updated execution state is announced to assistive technology in a timely way, and the analyst can identify that the same request has moved to completed without resubmitting.

steps.action: Navigate by landmarks, headings, and table commands to the completed results content.
steps.expectedResult: The results table is exposed semantically as a table with discernible column headers, and the request identifier is announced as labeled metadata associated with the request.

steps.action: Move to the query context section using screen reader navigation and read its contents.
steps.expectedResult: The query context control has an accessible name, its expanded or collapsed state is conveyed, and the content announces executed SQL text or summary and source object references in a readable order.

steps.action: Open the separate approved request that is configured to fail or exceed the normal response window.
steps.expectedResult: The screen reader announces a clear non-technical failure or delay message along with the request identifier, and no completed-results table is announced for that request.

steps.action: Review the failed or delayed view for any technical leakage in announced content.
steps.expectedResult: No database credentials, connection details, or low-level technical error text are exposed through the UI or screen reader output.

postconditions: The completed request remains available with accessible status, table, and query context content.
The failed or delayed request remains associated with a user-safe message and requestId only, without partial final results.
No sensitive database connection details are exposed visually or through assistive technology.

accessibility.title: Verify readability and operability of the results interface at 200% zoom and with adequate visual distinction for status and table content
preconditions: User is authenticated as an Automotive Reporting Analyst with access to an approved request that completes successfully and displays a results table with multiple columns.
A supported desktop browser is available with browser zoom controls and developer tools or contrast-check tooling available if needed.
The completed request includes visible execution status, request metadata, sortable table headers, and query context content.

steps.action: Open the interactive results page for the completed request at 100% browser zoom and note the placement of status, request metadata, results table, and query context.
steps.expectedResult: All major content areas are visible and distinguishable before zoom is applied.

steps.action: Increase browser zoom to 200% without changing the browser window to full-screen and review the page layout.
steps.expectedResult: Content remains readable and functional without text overlap, clipped labels, obscured controls, or loss of access to key information such as status, requestId, and query context.

steps.action: At 200% zoom, navigate to the results table and inspect header labels, row values, and sortable column controls.
steps.expectedResult: Table headers and row content remain legible, sortable controls remain identifiable, and horizontal or vertical scrolling, if present, does not prevent use of the table.

steps.action: Check the visual presentation of execution status indicators such as queued, running, completed, or failed and compare text against its background.
steps.expectedResult: Status information is not conveyed by color alone, accompanying text labels are visible, and foreground/background contrast is sufficient for users to distinguish the state.

steps.action: Open the query context section and verify readability of SQL summary text and source references at 200% zoom.
steps.expectedResult: The query context remains readable without truncating critical information, and controls or text do not overlap when expanded.

steps.action: Perform one table sort action and re-check page readability after the UI updates.
steps.expectedResult: The updated state remains visually clear at 200% zoom, with no hidden focus, clipped sort indicator, or layout break after interaction.

postconditions: The request remains completed and viewable at increased zoom.
The interface remains usable for reviewing status, metadata, query context, and sorted results without requiring reduced zoom.
No duplicate request execution is initiated during zoom or interaction checks.

security.title: Prevent access to results API with unauthenticated request
security.description: Verify the results and status endpoints reject requests that do not contain a valid authenticated session or bearer token, preventing identity spoofing and unauthorized retrieval of PostgreSQL reporting results.
preconditions: Results/status API endpoint is deployed in a test environment
At least one valid approved requestId exists
User session timeout/authentication mechanism is enabled

steps.action: Send a request to fetch query status/results using a valid requestId without any authentication token or session cookie.
steps.expectedResult: API rejects the request with 401 Unauthorized or equivalent and returns no result data, query context, or internal details.

steps.action: Repeat the request with an expired session cookie.
steps.expectedResult: Request is rejected and client is prompted to re-authenticate; no sensitive data is disclosed.

steps.action: Open the interactive results UI directly via bookmarked/deep-linked request URL in a logged-out browser session.
steps.expectedResult: UI redirects to login or shows unauthorized state without rendering result metadata or cached content.

postconditions: No unauthorized data is exposed
Security logs capture failed authentication attempts with request metadata

security.title: Reject forged or manipulated JWT/session token for result retrieval
security.description: Verify that forged, unsigned, weakly signed, or manipulated authentication tokens cannot be used to impersonate an Automotive Reporting Analyst and access result views.
preconditions: Application uses JWT or signed session token
Test users with different roles are available
A valid requestId exists for an authorized user

steps.action: Capture a valid token for an authorized analyst account in a test environment.
steps.expectedResult: Token is accepted only for the legitimate session.

steps.action: Modify token claims such as userId, role, domain, or expiration and resend the results/status request.
steps.expectedResult: Server detects invalid signature/claims and rejects the request.

steps.action: Attempt to use an unsigned token or a token signed with an incorrect key/algorithm.
steps.expectedResult: Server rejects the token and records the attempt in security logs.

steps.action: Attempt an algorithm confusion attack if JWT is used, such as altering alg header.
steps.expectedResult: Server ignores manipulated header values and denies access.

postconditions: No impersonation is possible through token manipulation
Audit/security logs contain token validation failures
security.testData: Valid JWT/session token; modified claims; unsigned token

security.title: Prevent spoofed backend status updates from rendering false completion state
security.description: Verify the UI accepts execution status transitions only from trusted backend channels and cannot be tricked into showing completed results via spoofed websocket, polling, or API responses.
preconditions: Application uses polling or push notifications for execution status
A request can be observed in queued/running state

steps.action: Intercept status polling or push traffic while a request is in progress.
steps.expectedResult: Traffic format and trust boundaries are identified.

steps.action: Attempt to inject or replay a fake 'completed' response with fabricated rows or metadata to the browser.
steps.expectedResult: UI ignores tampered or untrusted responses and does not render false results.

steps.action: Replay an old valid completion message for a different requestId.
steps.expectedResult: Client/server correlation checks reject mismatched requestId/session data.

postconditions: Only trusted server-originated status can update UI state
Replay/spoof events are logged or blocked
security.testData: In-progress requestId; captured historic completion payload

security.title: Detect tampering of requestId parameter to access or alter another analyst's result set
security.description: Verify requestId is immutable, validated server-side, and bound to the authenticated user/domain so attackers cannot tamper with identifiers in URLs, API bodies, or client storage to fetch unauthorized results.
preconditions: Two approved requests exist for different analysts or domains
Users have separate authorization scopes

steps.action: Log in as Analyst A and retrieve a valid requestId belonging to Analyst A.
steps.expectedResult: Results are accessible for Analyst A's own request.

steps.action: Modify the requestId in the results/status API call or browser URL to Analyst B's requestId.
steps.expectedResult: Server denies access with 403/404 and returns no data from Analyst B's request.

steps.action: Modify any hidden UI field, local storage value, or client-side state that references requestId and reload the page.
steps.expectedResult: Server-side authorization still prevents cross-request access; client-side tampering has no effect.

postconditions: Cross-request tampering is blocked
Authorization/audit logs show denied access attempts

security.title: Prevent manipulation of executionStatus or rowCount fields in API response
security.description: Verify UI and API integrity checks prevent tampered response fields such as executionStatus, rowCount, columns, or queryContext from misleading analysts or masking failure states.
preconditions: Proxy/interception tool is configured
A result request can be observed in transit

steps.action: Intercept a valid response for a failed or running request and alter executionStatus to 'completed'.
steps.expectedResult: Client or server validation detects inconsistent payload and avoids rendering completed state.

steps.action: Alter rowCount, columns, or rows to mismatched values and forward the response.
steps.expectedResult: UI rejects malformed/inconsistent payload and shows safe error state instead of misleading data.

steps.action: Alter queryContext to reference a different schema/table than executed.
steps.expectedResult: Integrity validation prevents display of untrusted or inconsistent context.

postconditions: Tampered response data is not trusted by the UI
Errors are handled without exposing raw payload details

security.title: Ensure sorting and filtering parameters cannot tamper with backend query behavior beyond approved scope
security.description: Verify interactive table sort or pagination parameters are strictly allowlisted and cannot alter approved SQL semantics, target unauthorized columns, or inject query modifiers.
preconditions: Interactive results view supports sorting/pagination
Known column names exist in the result set

steps.action: Invoke sort on a valid displayed column through the UI.
steps.expectedResult: Sorting works only on allowed result columns and remains within the approved request scope.

steps.action: Manipulate sort field parameter to a non-displayed, sensitive, or SQL fragment value via intercepted request.
steps.expectedResult: Server rejects unsupported values and does not alter executed query beyond the approved result handling.

steps.action: Manipulate pagination or ordering parameters with extreme or malformed values.
steps.expectedResult: Input is validated and request is safely rejected or normalized.

postconditions: Only allowlisted result interaction parameters are accepted
No hidden data fields become exposed through tampered sort/filter input

security.title: Audit log captures access to result view with requestId and user identity
security.description: Verify all result/status access events are logged with user identity, requestId, timestamp, action, status transition, and outcome so users cannot repudiate having viewed or attempted to access report results.
preconditions: Audit logging is enabled
A SIEM/log viewer or secure log store is accessible to testers

steps.action: Log in as an authorized analyst and open a result view for a valid requestId.
steps.expectedResult: An audit entry is created with user ID, requestId, action type, timestamp, and successful outcome.

steps.action: Refresh the status view during queued/running/completed states.
steps.expectedResult: Status transition or polling accesses are logged according to design without excessive omission.

steps.action: Verify logs are immutable or access-controlled and not editable by the analyst.
steps.expectedResult: Analyst cannot alter or delete audit records.

postconditions: Traceable audit evidence exists for result access
Logs are stored securely and protected from modification

security.title: Record denied access and suspicious token manipulation attempts
security.description: Verify failed authentication, authorization denial, and malformed token/requestId tampering attempts are captured in security logs with sufficient context for forensic investigation without exposing sensitive values.
preconditions: Security logging is enabled
Invalid token and unauthorized requestId are available for testing

steps.action: Attempt to access results using an invalid or manipulated token.
steps.expectedResult: Access is denied and a security log is generated with reason code and source context.

steps.action: Attempt to access another user's requestId while authenticated.

userStoryObject.title: As an Automotive Reporting Analyst, I want query results returned through an interactive interface with status feedback so that I can review PostgreSQL data efficiently and trust the reporting outcome
userStoryObject.description:
CONTEXT & BACKGROUND:

This story completes the LLM-driven automotive reporting workflow by delivering PostgreSQL query outcomes through an interactive interface rather than leaving the analyst at intent interpretation alone. The Automotive Reporting Analyst needs visible execution feedback and explainable result presentation to trust the reported vehicle, dealer, warranty, service, or related automotive data returned by the platform.

CURRENT STATE:

The platform intent workflow exists conceptually, but result delivery and status communication are incomplete or inconsistent. Analysts may not know whether a PostgreSQL request is still running, has failed, or has produced data tied to the executed SQL, which reduces confidence in the reporting outcome and slows review.

DESIRED STATE:

After an approved interpreted request is executed, the analyst can open a single interactive results experience that shows processing status, final tabular data, and query context linked to the executed SQL and source data references. The user receives timely feedback, can review returned rows efficiently, and can distinguish completed results from failed or still-running requests.

KEY FUNCTIONALITY:

• Render PostgreSQL query results in an interactive results view with sortable tabular output and request-level metadata.

• Show execution status updates such as queued, running, completed, and failed within the same interface.

• Associate displayed results with the executed SQL text or summary and source schema/table or view context.

• Return user-safe failure or delay messaging with a request identifier when execution does not complete normally.


USER INTERACTION FLOW:

1. The Automotive Reporting Analyst submits or opens an approved reporting request from the AI query workflow.

2. The interface displays an initial processing state while the platform starts PostgreSQL execution.

3. The system updates the visible status to queued or running and refreshes the request state without duplicate submission.

4. When execution completes, the interface replaces the status view with interactive results and supporting query context.

5. The analyst reviews returned rows, column headings, row count, and execution details tied to the request.

6. If execution fails or takes too long, the interface shows a clear status or error message and the request identifier instead of presenting incomplete output as final.


TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS:

• Data source: approved PostgreSQL reporting queries and execution metadata returned by the governed query service.

• Validation: only approved interpreted requests with a valid requestId may be fetched; result payloads must include columns, rows, executionStatus, requestId, and queryContext before the UI renders the completed state.

• Security: require authenticated session and enforce RBAC so users can view only results for domains and requests they are authorized to access; never expose database connection details in API or UI responses.

• Observability: log requestId, status transitions, execution duration, result row count, and failure codes to support audit and troubleshooting.

• Performance: support status or result response within the 10-second SLA for successful requests under normal load and use polling or push updates that avoid excessive backend calls.


OUT OF SCOPE:

• Direct SQL authoring or editing by the analyst.

• Dashboard building, report scheduling, and data export formats beyond the interactive results view.

• Changes to intent interpretation, SQL generation rules, or PostgreSQL schema design.


SUCCESS METRICS:

• At least 95% of successfully completed requests show a status update or final result within 10 seconds.

• 100% of completed result views include request-linked query context for executed SQL and source references.

• Reduction in analyst re-submissions caused by unclear execution state, measured by duplicate request attempts per session.

Persona: Automotive Reporting Analyst (Automotive Reporting Analyst)
userStoryObject.acceptanceCriteria:
1. When an approved interpreted request is submitted, the platform retrieves data from PostgreSQL and renders the returned rows in an interactive results view without exposing raw database credentials, direct SQL editing controls, or unrestricted database access.

2. For at least 95% of successfully completed requests under normal operating conditions, the user receives either a processing status update or the final results within 10 seconds of submission.

3. The interactive interface displays the execution state for each request as queued, running, completed, or failed, and updates the visible state without requiring the user to resubmit the request.

4. Completed results include query context that ties the displayed output to the executed SQL and source PostgreSQL objects so the analyst can understand how the reporting outcome was produced.

5. If query execution fails or exceeds the normal response window, the interface shows a non-technical status or error message with the request identifier and does not display partial or misleading final results as complete.
